title: OpenTitan IP blocks (upstream)
_note: UPSTREAM lowRISC OpenTitan's IP library, swept per module.  test/opentitan_equiv already sweeps ONE of its 45 blocks (OTBN, 32 modules, from a vendored copy); this family covers the library -- hw/ip, hw/ip_templates and top_earlgrey's generated IP -- which is 774 RTL files that nothing here measured.  Pinned at the SAME commit the caliptra-ss family already fetches (f49474bc), so this adds no new pin.  Pavona is a hard FORK whose RTL has diverged (of the 120 files the two trees share only 66 are byte-identical), so a pavona verdict is not an upstream verdict even for a block both have.  `prim_generic` is the technology library every abstract prim resolves to, and prim/rtl is on the include path for the assertion / flop macros OpenTitan relies on at compilation-unit scope.  SYNTHESIS compiles out the SVA macros, which is what OpenTitan's own flows pass and what run_opentitan_equiv.sh already does.

exclude_notes.^prim_xilinx: vendor technology libraries -- prim_generic is the one an abstract prim resolves to here; two implementations of the same prim in one closure are duplicate module definitions
exclude_notes.^prim_asap7: same: an ASAP7 technology library, not the generic one
exclude_notes.^ast$: the analog model is a behavioural stub, not synthesisable RTL (the same exclusion caliptra-ss makes)
exclude_notes.exclude_srcs: prim_asap7 / prim_xilinx*: the VENDOR technology libraries, excluded as SOURCES and not merely as module rows: their cells (BUFx2_ASAP7_75t_R, DFFA, Xilinx primitives) have no definition in the closure, and read_uhdm correctly refuses an instance of a module nobody defines -- rv_timer failed that way on the first run.  prim_generic is the technology library an abstract prim resolves to here.
exclude_notes.roots: hw/vendor/pulp_riscv_dbg + pulp_c: CLOSURE, not sweep targets (sweep_paths keeps the rows to OpenTitan's own IP): rv_dm and lc_ctrl's JTAG TAP are built over the vendored RISC-V debug module, so without dm_pkg read_slang reports "unknown class or package 'dm'" and lc_ctrl's DMI ports collapse to 1 bit and then drive constants.  pulp_common_cells is what that debug module is built on.
exclude_notes.roots: top_earlgrey/rtl/autogen/testing: lc_ctrl's life-cycle TOKENS live in a generated, top-specific package (`lc_ctrl_token_pkg`), so without this directory read_slang reports "unknown package 'lc_ctrl_token_pkg'" and the row has no reference.
exclude_notes.exclude_srcs: dmi_bscane_tap.sv: a XILINX-only FPGA JTAG tap in the vendored debug module: it instantiates the hard macro `BSCANE2`, which no generic closure defines, and it is an ALTERNATIVE to the tap the generic flow uses rather than something the design needs.  Leaving it in cost lc_ctrl and rv_dm their read_slang reference ("unknown module 'BSCANE2'").
exclude_notes.^chip_earlgrey_ / ^top_earlgrey$ / ^earl: CHIP tops, not IP blocks: this family's scope is the IP library, and a chip top needs its analog model and pad ring, which are deliberately not in this closure (`chip_earlgrey_asic` elab-fails for exactly that reason).  The chip top has its own route -- test/opentitan_equiv/scripts/fusesoc_closure.py resolves `lowrisc:systems:top_earlgrey` to 635 files with 0 unresolved cores and read_uhdm reads it clean -- and wants its own sharded workflow because the read alone peaks at 11.9 GB.
